newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico cuts May crude price differentials - PEMEX.
newsitem.headline: Mexico cuts May crude price differentials - PEMEX.

text.p: Mexico cut Thursday its May price differentials for crude oils by up to 50 cents to the United States, Europe and the Far East, a source from the trading arm of state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said.

Pemex term crude contract prices are based on formulas comprised of weighted price ratios of crudes and products in the region with a constant, or differential, which is generally updated monthly to reflect market conditions.
Pemex dropped its price of Maya heavy crude in May to the United States by 50 cents, its price of light Isthmus by 35 cents and of extra-light Olmeca by 50 cents.
For customers in Europe, Pemex cut May differentials for Maya crude by 50 cents and Isthmus by 50 cents.
In the Far East, Maya price differentials were cut 10 cents and Isthmus 10 cents, according to the source who declined to be named.
For current worldwide crude oil contract prices, please type OSP/O f9 on the Reuter's terminal.
Pemex has been looking to diversify and be more competitive in marketing its crude, in the face of its own increased output for the year and competition from Latin American competitor Venezuela.
Sour crude prices have been strengthening lately on pent up buying, but are still relatively feeble, traders said.

In March Mexico exported 770,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Maya to North America, 220,000 bpd to Europe and 7,000 bpd to the Far East. Isthmus exports to North America were 104,000, 22,000 to Europe and 48,000 to the Far East, while Olmeca exports to North America were 501,000 bpd.
